title: Proof of eos borromean cfl
html:
Proof. Proof of eos borromean cfl

Proof. The energy density and pressure follow from the standard non-relativistic Fermi gas formulas, with the mass parameter set by the algebraic-quantum-volume form of the topological mass formula. In the Borromean phase, M_B = \mathrm{Vol}_q(\beta_B) / \hbar_q^2 is the algebraic quantum-volume contribution (an element of \mathbb{Z}[q^{\pm 1/2}]). Its \tau-image forms the hyperbolic volume of the Borromean rings complement. In the CFL phase, M_D = (q + q^{-1})/3 is the crossing-energy contribution per quark (three quarks per baryon), and \mathrm{Vol}_q(\beta_{\mathcal{L}_H}) = 0 in \mathbb{Z}[q^{\pm 1/2}]. The algebraic quantum volume vanishes identically for the CFL Hopf-link braid, eliminating the volume term without invoking the geometric (3-manifold) interpretation.

The stiffness ratio follows immediately from P \propto n^{5/3}/M. At equal density, P_D / P_B = (M_B / M_D) \cdot 3^{5/3} (the 3^{5/3} arises from n_q = 3 n_B in the CFL quark gas).

The conformal limit c_s^2 \to 1/3 follows from the ultra-relativistic limit of the Fermi gas. When E_F \gg M, \varepsilon \approx 3P and c_s^2 = dP/d\varepsilon = 1/3. The CFL phase reaches this at moderate density because M_D is small. The Borromean phase requires E_F \sim 749 Skein units, corresponding to unphysical compression. \square
